name: digest
resume: All nine exports are done, including ascii serialization. utils is not a package here: packageVersion is the string 0.6.39, and head and tail only drop PKCS padding. There is no crate. Binary hashes skip the 14-byte header. Ascii hashes skip through the fourth newline.

functions.name: digest
functions.done: Hashes a serialized R object or raw bytes. Version 2 serialization skips the 14-byte header. ascii=TRUE writes the same objects as text and skips through the fourth newline. md5, sha1, sha256, and sha512 use hashlib. crc32 uses zlib. The other algorithms are written in Python.

proof.r:
suppressPackageStartupMessages(library(digest))
obj <- list(LETTERS, data.frame(a = letters[1:5], b = matrix(1:10, ncol = 2)))
one <- function() digest(obj)
value <- one()
elapsed <- numeric(20)
for (i in seq_len(20)) {
  t0 <- as.numeric(Sys.time())
  one()
  elapsed[[i]] <- as.numeric(Sys.time()) - t0
}
cat(sprintf("%s\n%.17g\n", value, median(elapsed) * 1000))
proof.python:
import statistics
import time

from digest import character, data_frame, digest, integer_matrix

obj = [
    character(list("ABCDEFGHIJKLMNOPQRSTUVWXYZ")),
    data_frame(
        a=character(list("abcde")),
        b=integer_matrix(list(range(1, 11)), ncol=2),
    ),
]


def one():
    return digest(obj)


value = one()
elapsed = []
for _ in range(20):
    started = time.perf_counter()
    one()
    elapsed.append((time.perf_counter() - started) * 1000)
print(value)
print("%.17g" % statistics.median(elapsed))

functions.name: digest2int
functions.done: Jenkins one-at-a-time hash of each string. A byte above 127 is a signed char, a zero byte ends the key, and the uint32 result is a signed 32-bit int. None is NA_character_ and hashes as the bytes of "NA".

check.case: digest2int("The quick brown fox jumps over the lazy dog", 0L)

proof.r:
suppressPackageStartupMessages(library(digest))
x <- "The quick brown fox jumps over the lazy dog"
invisible(digest2int(x, 0L))
elapsed <- numeric(20)
for (i in seq_len(20)) {
  t0 <- Sys.time()
  result <- digest2int(x, 0L)
  elapsed[i] <- as.numeric(difftime(Sys.time(), t0, units = "secs"))
}
med <- median(elapsed)
cat(sprintf("r_ms %.17g\n", med * 1000))
cat(sprintf("result %d\n", result))
proof.python:
import statistics
import time

from digest.digest2int import digest2int

x = "The quick brown fox jumps over the lazy dog"
digest2int(x, 0)
elapsed = []
result = None
for _ in range(20):
    t0 = time.perf_counter()
    result = digest2int(x, 0)
    elapsed.append(time.perf_counter() - t0)
med = statistics.median(elapsed)
print(f"py_ms {med * 1000:.17g}")
print(f"result {result[0]}")

functions.name: getVDigest
functions.done: Returns a function that hashes each element through digest. raw is always off. An integer vector is hashed one value at a time. warn returns NA and silent returns None.

proof.r:
suppressPackageStartupMessages(library(digest))
sha1 <- getVDigest(algo = "sha1")
one <- function() sha1(letters)
value <- one()
elapsed <- numeric(20)
for (i in seq_len(20)) {
  t0 <- as.numeric(Sys.time())
  one()
  elapsed[[i]] <- as.numeric(Sys.time()) - t0
}
cat(sprintf("%.17g\n", median(elapsed) * 1000))
cat(paste(value, collapse = "\n"), "\n", sep = "")
proof.python:
import statistics
import time

    one()

functions.name: hmac
functions.done: RFC 2104 HMAC. The key is padded to 64 bytes, 4 for crc32 and 128 for sha512, then digest is called twice. A prefix such as sha5 is resolved after the block size is chosen, so that call still uses a 64-byte block. A crc32 key longer than 4 bytes keeps the first byte of the raw digest.

functions.name: makeRaw
functions.done: charToRaw for a string, identity for bytes, hex pairs for a digest, and as.raw for numbers. A character vector longer than one warns and keeps the first string. hmac calls make_raw_digest on the hex hash.

functions.name: AES
functions.done: AES-128, AES-192, and AES-256 in ECB, CBC, CFB, and CTR. PKCS#7 padding is only allowed in CBC. CTR adds one to the IV as a 128-bit big-endian integer after copying it.

proof.r:
.libPaths(c("/home/ahmed/R/x86_64-pc-linux-gnu-library/4.5", .libPaths()))
suppressPackageStartupMessages(library(digest))
stopifnot(as.character(packageVersion("digest")) == "0.6.39")
hextextToRaw <- function(text) {
  vals <- matrix(as.integer(as.hexmode(strsplit(text, "")[[1]])), ncol=2, byrow=TRUE)
  vals <- vals %*% c(16, 1)
  as.raw(vals)
}
plaintext <- hextextToRaw("00112233445566778899aabbccddeeff")
key <- hextextToRaw("000102030405060708090a0b0c0d0e0f")
one <- function() {
  aes <- AES(key)
  aes$encrypt(plaintext)
}
value <- one()
elapsed <- numeric(20)
for (i in seq_len(20)) {
  t0 <- as.numeric(Sys.time())
  one()
  elapsed[[i]] <- as.numeric(Sys.time()) - t0
}
cat(sprintf('{"hex":"%s","median_ms":%.17g}\n', paste(sprintf("%02x", as.integer(value)), collapse=""), median(elapsed) * 1000))
proof.python:
import statistics
import time

from digest.aes import AES

key = bytes.fromhex("000102030405060708090a0b0c0d0e0f")
plaintext = bytes.fromhex("00112233445566778899aabbccddeeff")


def one():
    return AES(key).encrypt(plaintext)


value = one()
elapsed = []
for _ in range(20):
    started = time.perf_counter()
    one()
    elapsed.append((time.perf_counter() - started) * 1000)
print('{"hex":"%s","median_ms":%.17g}' % (value.hex(), statistics.median(elapsed)))
